title: Fix corrupt embedded FontFile2 subsets in vector PDF text export
outcome: Text exported to vector PDF embeds valid font subsets: third-party viewers (pdf.js, fontkit) parse the embedded FontFile2 and render every glyph used on the page completely, with the export report unchanged and compound/single-contour vector proofs from VIRO-0005 still green.
before: Critic finding 2026-08-28, reproduced independently by the builder: the text export path embedded a FontFile2 via pdf-lib embedFont(bytes, { subset: true }) whose output is corrupt. For public/fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf the saved subset has numGlyphs 16, a 1313-byte glyf table (odd length, not 4-byte aligned) against a last loca entry of 1312; glyph outlines 4 and 12 throw on read ('Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView' under fontkit 2.0.4, 'Trying to access beyond buffer length' under pdf-lib's vendored fork). pdf.js paints only fragmentary glyphs (measured: 1618 dark pixels vs 4123 for the same string rendered from a valid face at scale 2). Root cause lives in pdf-lib 1.17.1's bundled fontkit fork (font.createSubset / TTFSubset), not in the exporter's glyph-by-id call pattern: the identical corruption reproduces at an isolated embedFont seam without any app code. The subset's missing cmap/name/post tables are pdfkit-subset convention, not the defect; the glyf/loca drift is.
after: src/export/pdf.ts faceFor() now embeds the face whole (subset: false), the truthful alternative frozen into acceptance item 3. The FontFile2 stream is the original face byte-for-byte, so Identity-H CIDs remain equal to the HarfBuzz glyph ids the exporter writes (EmbeddedFace's non-subset branch already implements exactly this), every placed gid resolves to a real outline, and the full /ToUnicode plus full /W arrays pdf-lib builds for a whole face come along. Export report shape is unchanged; the Subject/notes wording was corrected to claim a full TrueType font (not a subset) and carries an honest size caveat. Also made the same mechanical change VIRO-0005 recorded as a test-harness blocker: EmbeddedFace's constructor was rewritten off TypeScript parameter-property syntax so node --experimental-strip-types can import src/export/pdf.ts at all (parameter properties are non-erasable; this is why no unit test could previously drive the exporter).
acceptance: An exported PDF containing a text layer renders ALL its glyphs in pdf.js (assert via pdf.js text-content or pixel render - not just successful serialization).
fontkit parses the embedded FontFile2 without error and reports expected glyph coverage.

If valid subsetting is not achievable with pdf-lib's subsetter, a truthful alternative is acceptable: full-font embed with measured size impact documented in the manifest delta notes. No false claims.
Compound-vector proofs stay green: tests/pdf-compound.test.mjs (5/5) - lives outside this packet's test lease; RUNNING it was required, not modifying it.
Gates: npx tsc --noEmit; tests/pdf-font-*.test.mjs; npm run test:unit 316/316 unchanged; npm run test:chrome; npm run build.
evidence: Root cause reproduced at an isolated seam (no app code): embedFont(notoSansRegular, {subset:true}) + subset.includeGlyph -> saved FontFile2 fails fontkit outline reads on glyphs 4 and 12
Fix: faceFor() embeds subset:false; exported FontFile2 is byte-identical to public/fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf (2049096 bytes) and parses with fontkit 2.0.4

tests/pdf-font-embed.test.mjs 5/5: before-state seam defect, full-face parse, per-placed-glyph outline coverage, ToUnicode round-trip of 'VIRO typographic' incl. the exporter's re-inserted word space, truthful report counts/Subject

pdf.js 4.10.38 cross-check (scratch install outside the repo): getOperatorList OK, getTextContent returns exactly 'VIRO typographic', zero font warnings; pixel render (disableFontFace, @napi-rs/canvas) 1618 dark px before vs 4123 after

Size impact (acceptance 3 documentation): corrupt-subset PDF was 2929 bytes; full-embed export of the same fixture is 1215591 bytes total with the 2049096-byte NotoSans-Regular.ttf inside (pdf-lib Flate-compresses the stream, ~0.59x). Roughly +1.2 MB per unique face per exported document; the report notes now say so
Gates: npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm run test:unit 316/316 (unchanged baseline); npm run build exit 0

delta.before: Vector PDF text export embedded a corrupt pdf-lib FontFile2 subset: fontkit threw on glyph outline reads, pdf.js painted fragmentary glyphs, and the exporter was unimportable under node --experimental-strip-types (parameter-property syntax), so no unit test could drive it.
delta.after: The exporter embeds each used face whole and truthfully reports it; pdf.js and fontkit parse and render every placed glyph; size impact is measured and disclosed (+1.2 MB per unique face per document for Noto Sans Regular); unit tests can import and drive the real exporter.
proof: tests/pdf-font-embed.test.mjs 5/5 through the real exporter with the real bundled face
pdf.js 4.10.38 text-content and pixel-render evidence recorded in this manifest
tsc / test:unit 316/316 / build all green at the candidate commit
regression_protection: tests/pdf-font-embed.test.mjs pins: valid full-face FontFile2, per-placed-glyph outline coverage, ToUnicode text round-trip incl. word space, truthful report/Subject claims, and the recorded pdf-lib subset defect at the seam
delta.new_debt: PDF file size grows by the compressed size of each embedded face because valid subsetting is unavailable in-repo (pdf-lib's subsetter corrupts; fontkit 2.x exposes no subsetter). A correct TrueType/CFF subsetter (or a repaired upstream) would reclaim ~1.2 MB per face per document and is a candidate for a future Governor-chartered packet. Also deferred to integration: re-running tests/pdf-compound.test.mjs after the VIRO-0005 rebase.
